summary: Orchestrator restart replays pending funcalls; delegation JWT-derived idempotency keys reused causing duplicate external webhook tool executions
description:
Issue summary:
AtlasForge runs a TypeScript orchestration service (long-running) in our Private deployment. The orchestrator issues delegation JWTs (short-lived signed tokens) and derives per-tool idempotency keys using a mix of the delegation_jwt.kid and an in-memory sequence counter. After an orchestrator process restart (caused by an autoscale event), the orchestrator restores a Redis checkpoint but the in-memory sequence counter is reset to the last persisted value which can be identical to the previous pre-restart values because the persistence checkpoint is slightly stale. When the regenerated idempotency key collides with the earlier value, downstream tool/webhook receives a second execution (duplicate side-effect).

Impact:
- Customer reports duplicated external webhook posts for time-sensitive payments/workflow steps (2-3 duplicates observed).
- Billing/side-effects: duplicate downstream jobs created; customer had to apply compensating actions manually.
- Repro rate: intermittent (observed after orchestrator restarts during heavy load).

Environment:
- Redwood Private on-premise cluster (k8s) with our private control plane; orchestrator service runs in us-east-2 region nodes.
- Orchestrator persists checkpoints to Redis (single-node primary with async snapshotting).
- SDK: redwood-js v2.4.1 (TypeScript) using streaming + AbortController for partial retries.
- Auth: delegation JWTs minted by AtlasForge auth service, short TTL (30s), rotated per-orchestrator-session.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start long-running orchestrator; run a multi-step orchestration that issues funcalls which POST to external webhook endpoints (payment gateway simulator).
2) Orchestrator persists checkpoint every 5s to Redis and increments in-memory sequence counter for idempotency key derivation.
3) Trigger a controlled restart (kubectl rollout restart) or autoscaler evicts pod while some funcalls are inflight.
4) After restart, orchestrator resumes from Redis checkpoint; it reuses delegation JWT (or requests a new JWT with the same kid) and sequence counter replays same numeric values for the next few actions.
5) External webhook receives duplicate POSTs (same payload semantics) for actions that had earlier been delivered but the orchestrator did not have the confirmed state persisted before the crash.

Observed logs/snippets (customer scrubbed):
- orchestrator-log: "INFO funcall:start idemp_key=dkid:42 seq=317"
- webhook-log: "200 OK processed event run_id=abc123 action=charge status=created"
- orchestrator-log (post-restart): "INFO resumed from checkpoint seq=317 delegation_kid=dkid"
- orchestrator-log: "INFO funcall:start idemp_key=dkid:42 seq=318"
- webhook-log: "200 OK processed event run_id=abc123 action=charge status=created"
(duplicate side-effect for run_id=abc123 observed)

Investigation notes so far (Support/SRE):
- Hypothesis A: Idempotency key construction mixes delegation_jwt.kid and in-memory counter; because Redis checkpoint is slightly stale and sequence persisted after webhook ack but before durable confirm, restart can replay the same key.
- Hypothesis B: Delegation JWT rotation reused same kid for newly minted tokens, leaving part of the idempotency namespace ambiguous across sessions.
- Confirmed: External webhook does not return a canonical idempotency token to the orchestrator — orchestration relies on local key derivation.
- Confirmed: Redis snapshotting frequency + async persistence means last-ack state may not be durable at the time of crash.
- Reproduced in staging with a local harness by accelerating restarts; duplicates observed consistently when restart happens within the persistence window.

Immediate customer workaround suggested and applied:
- Add explicit per-funcall idempotency_key parameter when invoking redwood funcalls (generate a UUID client-side per logical action and persist it to Redis before calling). This prevents reuse even if the orchestrator restarts.
- Increase Redis durability: enable AOF (append-only file) or increase checkpoint frequency so confirmed-acks are durable before process termination.
- As a temporary mitigation, orchestrator team paused aggressive pod evictions and increased rollout grace period.

Recommended long-term fixes (engineering):
1) SDK/orchestrator guidance: prefer explicit idempotency_key provided by the orchestration layer or client rather than implicit sequence-based keys. Document best-practices in the SDK docs for long-running orchestrations.
2) Orchestrator persistence: write-ahead persist "confirmed" state for tools before considering step complete (update checkpointing strategy to guarantee confirmed-ack durability).
3) Delegation JWT: ensure minted tokens have unique kid per session or include a stable run_id in the idempotency namespace to avoid collisions when JWT kids are reused.
4) Add optional server-side de-duplication header: Redwood could accept an authoritative idempotency header that the serving runtime enforces globally for private deployments (requires infra change).

Related artifacts and notes:
- Customer can provide minimal reproducer (we have staging capture).
- Customer impact deadline: manual compensating work ongoing; requests priority handling.

Next steps:
- SRE: collect fuller traces from Redis around checkpoint times (ACTION: Liam).
- SDK docs: add note and examples to TS SDK about explicit idempotency_key for orchestrations (ACTION: SDK docs owner).
- Internal: evaluate adding a server-side opt-in dedupe feature for Private (ticket: INT follow-up).

Resolution/ETA: Triage complete. Short-term mitigation implemented by customer (explicit idempotency keys + Redis AOF). Engineering follow-ups scheduled for prioritization.
